decisions.rationale: Fable 5 dual-use safeguards flag adversarial-security substance regardless of wording; renaming helps the static skill file but the actual adversarial RUN still trips (and correctly hands off to Opus 4.8). The honest resolution is (a) a real constructive skill that stays on Fable because it is not adversarial, with an explicit handoff for the sensitive slice, and (b) delegating the adversarial slice to Opus subagents per Agent=Model+Harness. The scoping feature leverages the existing plugin-root skills/ (ships to consumers) vs .claude/skills/ (framework-only) delivery boundary; isFrameworkRepo guards prevent misuse in either direction. All 4 tickets clean-reviewed (0 HIGH, 0 RC), security invariants preserved in assimilate-current-project, no dangling consumer references. Refused to help defeat a safety classifier even for a benign end.

decisions.decision: Simplify tdd for developer velocity (human directive): (1) narrow the tier-assignment rubric to the LIGHTEST DEFENSIBLE tier — tdd reserved for security/parsing/schema/state-mutation, tests-after the default, uat-only for glue/docs (src/ absent-tier default stays tdd); (2) collapse the two-commit discipline to a SINGLE test+impl commit, KEEPING the captured red-run evidence as the tests-first proof and having the reviewer reproduce red by reverting/stashing impl hunks instead of checking out a prior test-only commit. Applied permanently across CLAUDE.md + orchestrator-routing SKILL.md + developer.md + reviewer.md (TASK-148, commit 912f32a) and used for every subsequent tdd ticket this run (141/143/149/150). Graph: decision-20260712-simplify-tdd-single-commit; task-148 produced-by it.
decisions.rationale: The red-run evidence (proof the tests failed for the right reason before impl) is the load-bearing anti-test-laundering signal and is preserved; the separate test:-before-impl commit was ceremony whose only extra value (a clean checkpoint to re-run red at) the reviewer already achieves by stashing the impl. The rubric narrowing is the bigger velocity lever — it uses the existing tests-after/uat-only tiers more, with zero rigor loss where tdd still applies. Human chose 'both simplifications, permanent' after being shown the tradeoff. The reviewer flagged (TASK-144) that a validation seam assigned tests-after would now be tdd under the narrowed rubric — recorded for future tier calls; coverage was tdd-equivalent so no risk materialized. Graph: decision-20260712-simplify-tdd-single-commit; task-148 produced-by it.
